text:
maria: Heads-up — CI eval run for quant-int8 bringup shows pass@k > 100% for some long-answer QA suites. Screenshot on dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dash/XYZ
sam: yikes, saw that alert. quick glance at raw logs shows duplicated generations in the candidate list.
alex: duped candidates can inflate pass@k if aggregation is wrong. which runner shard? job 7890
ci-bot: Job 7890 failed: eval-runner/shard-12 exited non-zero. Logs: https://ci.redwood/job/7890/console
maria: shard-12. example snippet from runner output:
```
candidates = ["A","A","B","C"]
pass_at_k(2) => counts matches across candidates -> 3/2 = 150%
```
sam: that's the gist — our pass@k impl is aggregating matches per-candidate but using per-sample denominator when merging shards, so numerators can exceed denominators across sharded sums.
priyanka: oof. also noticed fuzzy exact-match comparator is token-overlap-based but dedupe/normalization happens after scoring, so duplicates survive.
elaine: minimal repro I ran:
```
def fuzzy_match(pred, ref, thresh=0.7):
    ov = token_overlap(pred, ref)
    return ov >= thresh

# runner collects candidates per sample across n systems
matches = sum(fuzzy_match(c,r) for c in candidates)
# later when merging shards we did total_matches += matches
# but we kept sample_count += 1 instead of += num_samples_in_shard
```
alex: TL;DR two bugs: (1) shard aggregator is inconsistent — we sum per-candidate matches but only increment sample count once; (2) dedupe applied in wrong stage so repeated generations inflate candidate pool.
maria: propose fix: (A) compute pass@k per-sample (0/1) then aggregate sums of samples; (B) canonicalize/dedupe candidates before scoring; (C) add deterministic ordering in runner to avoid nondet dedupe flakiness.
priyanka: agree. also add unit test with synthetic shard that demonstrates >100 -> must assert <=100.
sam: created draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/452 — fixes aggregator and moves dedupe earlier. assigns alex to review.
alex: will review today. quick note: we need to preserve multi-candidate weight when using importance sampling for pass@k variants. I'll add comments in PR for importance-sampling path.
ci-bot: PR 452 opened by sam. Tests: 14/320 failing locally, 2 are timing flakes in smoke tests.
priyanka: for dashboards — we should add a guard in reporting to clip percentages to 100 and emit warning metric when clipping is necessary so we can detect earlier.
elaine: also propose a small metric change: add "soft_exact_k" that records per-sample max match across k candidates using fuzzy comparator instead of per-candidate counts. That will be easier to reason about and map to user expectations.
maria: good idea. can we add a migration step to backfill soft_exact_k for previous runs? maybe run on raw artifacts in S3, cost estimate?
alex: backfill feasible but heavy. let's ship fix first, then schedule a backfill for lower-priority historical windows.
priyanka: CI wiring: add a smoke test that runs a tiny synthetic dataset with seeded RNG and asserts deterministic pass@k numbers. This should catch ordering/dedupe regressions.
sam: I'll push updated tests in the PR, and add the dashboard clipping + warning metric in telemetry PR.
ci-bot: merge check: PR 452 — required reviewers: alex, maria. CI: pending.
maria: thanks. follow-up: update eval docs under docs/metrics/pass_at_k.md to explain dedupe semantics and fuzzy comparator tunables.
alex: noted. target deploy next week after CI green. :rocket:
